RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-3469ABE4FC-29435
Notice date: 2026-08-16
Requested service: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-12

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-16, Reference number POC-3469ABE4FC-29435. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

I understand that the plan's governing medical policy for this procedure is UnitedHealthcare's "Surgery of the Ankle" Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy, Policy Number 2026T0622O. That policy identifies CPT 27702 under the category "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle," and states the following coverage rationale, which I am quoting directly from the policy document:

"Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint); Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle; Arthrotomy, Ankle; Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

I note that this policy document itself does not spell out the specific InterQual clinical criteria elements (e.g., required findings, duration of conservative treatment, imaging thresholds); it incorporates the InterQual® CP "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" criteria by reference to a separate, proprietary resource that was not available to me. I have not been provided with the specific InterQual criteria applied to my case, and I am not able to quote that document because I have not seen it. I am therefore requesting, as part of this appeal and pursuant to my right to the criteria relied upon in this determination, that the plan provide me and my treating surgeon with a copy of the specific InterQual criteria used to deny this request, so that we may confirm point-by-point compliance. Below, I have addressed the clinical record against the general categories of evidence that InterQual and comparable payer policies for total ankle arthroplasty typically require (failed conservative care, imaging evidence of joint destruction, and functional impairment); I ask the reviewer to map these facts against the actual InterQual criteria applied to my case.

The clinical record submitted with my prior authorization request includes the following, which I believe supports medical necessity for total ankle replacement:

1. Chronicity and severity of symptoms: I have experienced 9 months of progressive ankle pain that is unrelieved by rest.

2. Failed conservative treatment:
   - Supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, 16 weeks (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03), 24 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
   - Corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-14, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.

3. Objective imaging findings: Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained 2026-06-28 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, consistent with end-stage ankle arthritis.

4. Functional impairment: I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to walking two blocks before symptoms prevent further ambulation.

5. Physical examination findings: Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

6. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

7. My treating surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist (orthopedic surgery), has determined that total ankle replacement is the appropriate surgical treatment based on this clinical picture.

Given the duration and severity of my symptoms, the extensive and unsuccessful trial of conservative treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection), the objective radiographic evidence of advanced joint destruction, and the significant functional limitation I experience, I respectfully request that the plan reverse its denial and authorize CPT 27702.

I am enclosing the following records in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03)
- Documentation of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-04-14)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report (2026-06-28)
- Office visit/examination notes documenting gait, range of motion, and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, MD

If any additional documentation is needed to complete this appeal, please contact me at the phone number or email address listed above, or contact my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone number].

I further request, in accordance with applicable law, a copy of the specific InterQual® CP "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" criteria that were applied to my request, so that I may respond to any specific elements not addressed above.

I look forward to your prompt reconsideration of this determination within the applicable appeal timeframe, and I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-12.

Sincerely,

Cameron Carter
